subject: On-prem POC credits and compliance evidence for MedIQ evaluation
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@mediqsys.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anika Sharma <security@mediqsys.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Feb 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: On-prem POC credits & SOC2 evidence for MedIQ evaluation

Hi Stephanie / Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team is comfortable with the architecture in principle, but they're gating the on-prem / VPC POC on two items before procurement will sign off: (1) an extension of trial credits specifically for an isolated on-prem evaluation so we can stress test token throughput with our dataset, and (2) a small set of compliance artifacts (SOC 2 summary, redacted infra diagram, and a short attestation on tenancy isolation).

Can Redwood provide a temporary credit allocation (we're estimating ~$25k–$40k worth of usage for a 4-week private POC) and a redacted SOC2 summary + confirmation that the private control plane option will not mix our workloads with multi-tenant hosts? Procurement is sensitive to any commingling language. If you need an NDA addendum or a short MOU, we can route that quickly.

We are aiming to kick off the POC the week of Feb 21 — is there a way to get an interim approval/promo so we don't slip?

Thanks,
Tom Ellis
Head of Infrastructure
MedIQ Systems
T: +1 415 555 0183

Attachments referenced: "mediq_poc_requirements.xlsx" (we'll send formally once you confirm path)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@mediqsys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 7 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: On-prem POC credits & SOC2 evidence for MedIQ evaluation

Tom — thank you, this is clear and helpful.

We can support an isolated on-prem / VPC POC and provide the compliance artifacts you requested. Immediate next steps we can take today:

- Provision a conditional promo credit pool: we can provision $30,000 in POC credits scoped to the "Private" tenancy option for 45 days. This is contingent on receipt of the SOC2 summary (we'll provide a redacted copy), a signed MOU or PO from MedIQ confirming limited-use terms, and a commitment to provide the small network diagram + contact for the infra team.
- Attachments I’m sending now: redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf (redacted), poc_credit_request_form.pdf (please sign the highlighted sections and return).
- If procurement needs additional wording about tenancy isolation, we can generate an addendum to the MOU stating: "MedIQ's workloads will run on dedicated private tenancy with no shared GPU host mixing for the duration of the POC."

Ben / Rishi — I’ve looped you both to request quick approval for the $30k conditional credit (deal RWIN-5239). If we approve, I'll attach the signed MOU and push the credit into MedIQ's trial account; we should also record this as a one-time promo in the billing system.

Tom — could you confirm the primary technical contact on your side for onboarding and whether legal would want us to sign a short MOU or route via your standard PO? If you can return the signed form this week we can lock the promo and be ready before Feb 21.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai | +1 510 555 0124

Attachments: redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf; poc_credit_request_form.pdf
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 7 Feb 2027 13:22:00 -08:00
Subject: INTERNAL — quick approval request: MedIQ private POC credits (RWIN-5239)

Ben / Rishi — quick context and ask so this doesn't block kickoff:

- Customer: MedIQ Systems (healthcare analytics) — security gating on tenancy isolation + SOC2 artifacts.
- Proposed promo: $30k credits scoped to "Private" tenancy for 45 days. Conditional on receiving signed poc_credit_request_form.pdf and the network diagram + MOU/PO.
- Why approve: timeline slip will push their pilot past the Q1 vendor selection window; MedIQ is likely to expand to Dedicated if POC goes well.
- Risk: low — credits are scoped & timeboxed; no default discount to list pricing and we require MOU/PO.

Suggested approval text if you’re comfortable: "Approve $30k private-tenancy POC credits for MedIQ (RWIN-5239). Condition: signed MOU/PO and receipt of redacted network diagram."

Please reply with a one-line approval so I can record in HubSpot and push credits.

Thanks —
Stephanie

(On a related note: Rishi — if legal needs to tweak tenancy language, happy to loop Laura in Legal, but keeping it simple keeps procurement moving)
From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@mediqsys.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anika Sharma <security@mediqsys.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 16:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: On-prem POC credits & SOC2 evidence for MedIQ evaluation

Stephanie — thanks for the fast turnaround and the redacted SOC2 summary.

We reviewed the terms with procurement and legal; MedIQ can sign a short MOU acknowledging the one-time POC credits and limited-use tenancy. Procurement would like the following language included in the MOU: "Redwood will provision dedicated private tenancy for MedIQ's POC such that no GPU host will host workloads from other customers for the duration of the POC." If that wording is acceptable, procurement can return a countersigned MOU by EOD Thursday.

We are okay with the $30k conditional credit you proposed. I've attached a redacted network diagram (mediq_network_diag.pdf) and put Anika Sharma from security on the thread for any follow-up questions. Our technical lead (cc'd in the next email) will coordinate onboarding and smoke tests.

Can you confirm: once the signed MOU and network diagram are received, what is the typical time-to-provision for the private tenancy and credits? We want to plan smoke tests and an initial throughput run.

Appreciate the help — this keeps us on track for the Feb 21 start.

Best,
Tom Ellis
Head of Infrastructure
MedIQ Systems

Attachments: mediq_network_diag.pdf
